title: Childhood & Adolescent Immunization Schedule
keywords: DTaP IPV Hib PCV rotavirus 2 4 6 months
sources: CDC/ACIP Recommended Child and Adolescent Immunization Schedule, United States, 2025

changelog.change: Initial entry — routine 0–18 y schedule by visit, adolescent platform, annual/seasonal products, and catch-up principles. Verify against the current-year CDC schedule before use.

summary: Routine US schedule by well-child visit. Vaccines can be co-administered at the same visit at separate sites. Minor illness, low-grade fever, and breastfeeding are not contraindications. Confirm doses and ages against the current-year CDC/ACIP schedule — this changes annually.

body.text: This is a reference snapshot (2025 schedule). ACIP updates it every year — check the current CDC schedule (and your state registry) for the definitive recommendation, minimum intervals, and any newly added products.

rows: DTaP #3 · Hib #3 (if a 4-dose product) · PCV #3 · rotavirus #3 (only if RotaTeq/RV5) · HepB #3 and IPV #3 may be given 6–18 mo · influenza annually from 6 mo
MMR #1 · varicella #1 · Hib booster · PCV #4 · HepA #1
Tdap ×1 · HPV series (2 doses if started at age 9–14, 0 and 6–12 mo; 3 doses if started at ≥ 15 y or immunocompromised) · MenACWY #1
MenACWY booster · MenB (shared clinical decision, 16–23 y; 2–3 doses depending on product)

items: Influenza: every year for everyone ≥ 6 months. First-ever season under age 9 → 2 doses ≥ 4 weeks apart.
COVID-19: per the current ACIP recommendation for age.

RSV prevention for infants: nirsevimab (monoclonal) for infants < 8 months entering their first RSV season, OR maternal RSVpreF vaccine at 32–36 weeks' gestation (Sept–Jan) — not both. A second nirsevimab dose in the second season for high-risk children 8–19 months.
Do NOT restart a series for a lapse — count doses already given and resume, respecting minimum intervals.
Minimum age and minimum interval (not the 'recommended' age) govern whether an early dose counts; a dose given > 4 days before the minimum is invalid and must be repeated.

Hib and PCV catch-up depends on the age at first dose — fewer doses are needed the later a healthy child starts, and neither is routinely needed after age 5 (Hib) / for healthy children after 24 months (PCV, unless a risk condition).
Rotavirus: maximum age for dose 1 is 14 weeks 6 days; series must be completed by 8 months 0 days — do not start late.
MMR and varicella: minimum interval between the two doses is 4 weeks.

body.text: Live vaccines (MMR, varicella, LAIV, rotavirus): give together on the same day or separate by ≥ 4 weeks. Defer live vaccines in significant immunosuppression, in pregnancy, and for ~11 months after high-dose IVIG/blood products (MMR/varicella). Rotavirus is contraindicated with a history of intussusception or SCID.
